title: runtime/telemetry: add wasted prefill metric + correlate with eviction/pressure
author: Samir Qureshi
release_notes: Adds cache telemetry for wasted prefill (prefill tokens not followed by cache reuse), with low-cardinality tags and optional correlation counters for eviction/pressure; gated behind cache telemetry flags + sampling.
description:
Motivation: We’ve had multiple investigations where KV/prefix cache hit-rate dropped, but we couldn’t quantify the *cost impact* on prefill. This PR introduces a first-pass metric for “wasted prefill”: prefill tokens that were computed but did not contribute to subsequent decode reuse because we missed/evicted/disabled caching. The goal is a privacy-safe, low-overhead signal we can correlate with cache pressure to (a) triage regressions and (b) power recommendations (e.g., increase max_prefix_cache_bytes, adjust TTL/eviction policy, fix version mismatch, or change routing locality).

Definition (per ADR-in-progress / sprint alignment):
- Wasted prefill tokens are counted per request at the end of prefill.
- For a given request, we compute: wasted_prefill_tokens = prefill_tokens - reused_tokens_observed.
- reused_tokens_observed is the number of prefill tokens that are attributable to prefix/KV reuse for the subsequent decode path of the same request.
- We intentionally bucket this at request-level and aggregate to avoid logging prompts or adding high-cardinality dimensions.

Implementation notes:
- Adds a new histogram: runtime.cache.wasted_prefill_tokens (buckets aligned to prompt-length bucket policy).
- Adds a companion counter: runtime.cache.wasted_prefill_requests_total with a miss_reason label (enum) to help separate “real misses” vs “cache disabled” vs “evicted/pressure”.
- Emits lightweight correlation counters when eviction/pressure is active during prefill: runtime.cache.wasted_prefill_eviction_correlated_total and runtime.cache.wasted_prefill_pressure_correlated_total (both low-cardinality, no per-tenant labels).
- Sampling: the histogram is sampled using the existing cache telemetry sampling knobs (default unchanged); counters remain unsampled but are kept low-cardinality.
- Avoids per-tenant, per-prompt hash, or request-id labels; uses allowlisted route/model/version tags via request context plumbing already in-flight.

Operational impact:
- Overhead: adds a couple of integer accumulators per request + single emission at prefill end; no per-token events.
- Can be used in dashboards to show wasted prefill alongside hit-rate and eviction/pressure, especially useful when workload mix changes make hit-rate alone ambiguous.

Testing:
- Unit tests for token accounting under (1) full miss, (2) partial reuse, (3) policy disabled, (4) eviction during prefill.
- Integration test extends the cache-metrics harness to assert wasted prefill > 0 on forced misses and ~0 on stable cache reuse.
- Perf: validated in perf-canary locally; no measurable p95 regression at default sampling.

Follow-ups (not in this PR):
- Fold this into the canonical metrics naming PR and dashboard panels (separate PRs).
- Improve semantics for streaming retries and batched prefill attribution (tracked separately).
commits: runtime/cache: add WastedPrefillAccumulator to request lifecycle
telemetry: emit wasted prefill histogram + request counter w/ miss_reason
runtime/cache: plumb eviction + pressure flags into prefill completion
tests: add unit tests for wasted prefill accounting and correlation
integration: extend cache metrics harness to validate wasted prefill behavior
docs: add short note to internal cache telemetry README
review_conversation:
Omar El-Sayed (review): Definition question: reused_tokens_observed — are we counting prefix cache reuse only, or KV cache reuse too? For multi-turn chat, this can be tricky if we extend the KV across turns.

Samir Qureshi (author): Counting both prefix cache and KV cache reuse, but only as observed/attributed during prefill->decode planning for the *same request*. I’m avoiding cross-request attribution in v1. For multi-turn chat, each turn is its own request; reuse is captured if the runtime reuses cached prefix/KV for that turn.

Noah Patel (review): The correlation counters seem a bit hand-wavy. Can we ensure they don’t become “always on” under high utilization and lose meaning? Also please confirm they don’t have route/model tags.

Samir Qureshi (author): Good point. I’m scoping correlation as “eviction occurred during this request’s prefill window” and “pressure gauge exceeded threshold during prefill window”. Tags are intentionally restricted to {deployment_mode, region} only. Added comments + tests asserting tag set.

Nadia Rahman (review): Naming: please align with our cache metrics naming conventions (runtime.cache.*). Also ensure histogram buckets match the prompt-length bucket policy.

Samir Qureshi (author): Updated names to runtime.cache.wasted_prefill_tokens + runtime.cache.wasted_prefill_requests_total. Histogram buckets now reuse the same bucket boundaries as prompt_len_bucket definitions; included in registry.

Marcus Reed (review): Perf: can you add a micro benchmark or at least a note about allocations? Observing histogram per request can allocate if tags aren’t stable.

Samir Qureshi (author): Verified tags come from a cached/arena-backed tag set; no per-request allocations beyond integer math. Added a perf note + ensured the tags are built once per request context.

Allison Grant (review): For dashboards, we’ll want to compare wasted prefill with eviction pressure. Can you include an explicit miss_reason for policy_disabled vs version_mismatch? That will help triage.

Samir Qureshi (author): Added miss_reason propagation in the counter path. Currently supports: capacity, ttl_expired, policy_disabled, hash_mismatch, version_mismatch, unknown. (Enum already shared with other cache metrics PRs.)

Omar El-Sayed (final approval): Looks good for v1. Please file a follow-up to reconcile semantics under streaming retries (we’ve seen double counting elsewhere).

Samir Qureshi (author): Filed follow-up and added a TODO with a link to the retry semantics ticket.
